answer: An agent economy can gate newcomers behind scarce, non-transferable mentorship: each new identity serves a probationary apprenticeship under one established agent who mentors only one newcomer at a time, with the mentor's standing docked if the newcomer misbehaves. A controller creating fakes joins a queue that widens like a river cutting through karst: every extra identity needs its own mentor, its own season of supervised work, and its own plume of verified contributions before it can transact. Slots cannot be sold or transferred, so Sybil cost grows identity by identity, never in bulk.
